title: Homeostasis
seo_title: Anatomy and Physiology 12: Homeostasis Worksheets (BC Curriculum)
short_title: feedback, nerves, hormones and the kidney
standard_text: Organ systems have complex interrelationships to maintain homeostasis: negative and positive feedback, the nervous system and nerve impulses, the endocrine system and hormones, blood glucose, temperature and water balance. (summary of BC's Curriculum, Anatomy and Physiology 12)
meta_desc: Free Anatomy and Physiology 12 worksheets (BC Curriculum): feedback, nerves, hormones and the kidney. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Nerves are fast; hormones are slower but last longer.
body_html:
How to think about it

Homeostasis is keeping internal conditions steady. In negative feedback, a change triggers a response that reverses it (sweating when hot). Positive feedback increases a change (contractions in childbirth).

Neurons carry electrical impulses; at a synapse a neurotransmitter crosses the gap. The endocrine system releases hormones into the blood: insulin lowers blood glucose and glucagon raises it; ADH makes the kidneys save water.

Example

Blood glucose rises after a meal. Which hormone is released?

From the pancreas

Answer: insulin

Example

Is shivering when cold negative or positive feedback?

It reverses the change.

Answer: negative

Common mistakes

  • Thinking positive feedback means 'good'.
  • Mixing up insulin and glucagon.
  • Thinking nerve signals jump the synapse electrically.
